value_stream.name: Energy Efficiency, Conservation & RA 11285 Compliance Program

fields.Participants: EEO, Sustainability (links to VS-25), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Procurement (links to VS-34), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Renewable (links to VS-108), Cross-Entity (links to VS-72), Compliance (links to VS-22), Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning (links to VS-33.1); RA 11285 obligation; program review

workflows.name: Energy Efficiency & Conservation Program Strategy & Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "EEO/Sustainability define the energy-efficiency & conservation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-renew of "EEO establish the governance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the program budget and ECM investment envelope" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-138 (ensure RA 11285 energy compliance & M&V integrity.)
- operational: EEO authority; operational: compliance map (W3738)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Energy managed reactively per-site with no program/DOE view; mitigated by EEO authority
- **Compliance-blindness risk**: RA 11285 obligations unknown/unmet; mitigated by compliance map (W3738)
System Touchpoints: - Sustainability/ESG (links to VS-25); facilities (links to VS-20.3); store ops (links to VS-07); procurement (links to VS-34); finance (links to VS-17.4); renewable (links to VS-108); compliance (links to VS-22); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: EEO/Sustainability define the energy-efficiency & conservation (EEC) program strategy and governance: scope (~205 sites — 200 stores, 4 DCs, HQ), the RA 11285 compliance map (designated-establishment status, energy audit, conservation plan, DOE reporting), the energy-management-system approach (ISO 50001 EnMS), the ECM investment strategy, and KPIs (energy intensity kWh/sqm, cost, audit compliance, ECM savings, GHG reduction)

EEO establish the governance: EEO authority, the energy team (Facilities, Store Ops, Procurement, Finance, Sustainability), cross-functional responsibilities, and integration to facilities (VS-20.3), ESG (VS-25), renewable (VS-108), procurement (VS-34), and compliance (VS-22)

Executive committee ratify the EEC strategy, approve the program budget and ECM investment envelope (links to W3743), and report energy posture to the executive risk/sustainability committee (links to VS-21.2/VS-25.3) and board (links to VS-36); communicate the mandate

fields.Participants: EEO, Compliance (links to VS-22), Sustainability (links to VS-25), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Cross-Entity (links to VS-72), Records (links to VS-88)
fields.Trigger: Program strategy (W3737); new site; threshold change

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-classify of "classify each site/entity under RA 11285 designated-establishment thresholds" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "maintain the designated-establishment record" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track obligation compliance per site/entity" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-138 (ensure RA 11285 energy compliance & M&V integrity.)
- operational: threshold-based classification; operational: deadline tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-classification risk**: A large site under-classified, missing obligations; mitigated by threshold-based classification
- **Registration-lapse risk**: DOE registration/reporting missed; mitigated by deadline tracking
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (links to VS-22); legal (links to VS-100.3); records (links to VS-88); cross-entity (links to VS-72); audit (links to VS-21); governance (links to W3737)

steps.activity: EEO/Compliance classify each site/entity under RA 11285 designated-establishment thresholds (Type 1: 500,000–4,000,000 kWh/yr; Type 2: >4,000,000 kWh/yr), determine the per-site and per-entity obligations (energy audit frequency, conservation plan, EEO designation, reporting), and register with DOE per the IRR

EEO/Compliance manage the DOE registration and designation lifecycle: submit the EEO designation, maintain the designated-establishment record, manage DOE designated-establishment registration and annual reporting via the DEOS portal, and respond to DOE inquiries

EEO/Compliance track obligation compliance per site/entity (audit due-dates, plan submission, reporting deadlines), report compliance status to governance (links to W3737/VS-22) and audit (links to VS-21), and manage any non-compliance corrective action

fields.Participants: EEO, Sustainability (links to VS-25), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Store Ops (links to VS-07), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), Procurement (links to VS-34), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Renewable (links to VS-108)

workflows.name: Energy Efficiency Officer, Energy Manager & Energy Team Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "reports to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-589 (ensure controlled execution — EEC Program Strategy, Designated-Establishment & Governance (PA-120.1).)
- operational: training/certification; operational: qualification; operational: site-level champions
Pain Points / Risks: - **Competency-gap risk**: EEO/Energy Manager lacks required qualification; mitigated by training/certification
- **Resourcing risk**: Program under-resourced vs ~205 sites; mitigated by site-level champions
System Touchpoints: - HR/L&D (links to VS-19.4/VS-103); sustainability (links to VS-25); facilities (links to VS-20.3); store ops (links to VS-07); procurement (links to VS-34); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: EEO/Sustainability/HR establish and maintain the energy-management organization: the EEO (statutorily designated under RA 11285), the Energy Manager (operational), and the cross-functional Energy Team (Facilities, Store Ops, Procurement, Finance, Sustainability); manage roles, competencies, and RA 11285-required qualifications

EEO/Sustainability manage energy-management competency and capacity: training/certification of the EEO/Energy Manager (links to VS-19.4), site-level energy champions at stores/DCs, and the energy-team operating cadence

EEO/Sustainability integrate the energy team to operations: ensure facility/store teams execute energy SOPs, energy considerations are embedded in facility/store operations (links to VS-20.3/VS-07), and the team reports to governance (links to W3737)

fields.Participants: EEO, Sustainability (links to VS-25), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Finance (links to VS-17.4), ESG (links to VS-25.3), Audit (links to VS-21), Renewable (links to VS-108)

workflows.name: Energy Policy, Targets & ISO 50001 Energy Management System

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-renew of "EEO/Sustainability maintain the energy policy and targets" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "EEO/Sustainability implement and maintain the ISO 50001 Energy Management" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "EEO/Audit assure the EnMS through internal audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-589 (ensure controlled execution — EEC Program Strategy, Designated-Establishment & Governance (PA-120.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-EnMS risk**: No systematic energy-management discipline; mitigated by ISO 50001 EnMS
- **Target-misalignment risk**: Energy targets not aligned to ESG/decarbonization; mitigated by integration
System Touchpoints: - Sustainability/ESG (links to VS-25); facilities (links to VS-20.3); GHG accounting (links to W192/W3466); renewable (links to VS-108); audit (links to VS-21); governance (links to VS-25.3)

steps.activity: EEO/Sustainability maintain the energy policy and targets: the energy-intensity reduction target (kWh/sqm), the renewable/clean-energy target (links to VS-108), the GHG-reduction contribution (links to VS-25/W192/W3466), and the ECM savings target; align to ESG/decarbonization strategy (links to VS-25.3)

EEO/Sustainability implement and maintain the ISO 50001 Energy Management System (EnMS): energy planning, energy review (significant energy uses - SEUs), energy performance indicators (EnPIs), baselines, objectives/targets, operational controls, and continual improvement; manage certification

EEO/Audit assure the EnMS through internal audit (links to VS-21) and management review, drive continual improvement (Plan-Do-Check-Act), and report EnMS performance and certification posture to governance (links to W3737/VS-25.3)

fields.Participants: EEO, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), IT/IoT (links to VS-27.2/VS-27.3), Sustainability (links to VS-25), Finance (links to VS-17.4), BI (links to VS-28.1), Store Ops (links to VS-07), DC Ops (links to VS-04)
fields.Trigger: EnMS implementation (W3740); data need; metering project

workflows.name: Energy Data, Metering & Energy Accounting Infrastructure

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "EEO/Facilities-IT deploy and maintain the energy-metering and data infrastructure" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate utility bills, allocate energy cost to sites/entities" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "EEO/BI assure energy-data quality" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-589 (ensure controlled execution — EEC Program Strategy, Designated-Establishment & Governance (PA-120.1).)
- operational: sub-metering rollout; operational: bill validation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-gap risk**: Unmetered/incomplete energy data undermines analytics/compliance; mitigated by sub-metering rollout
- **Bill-error risk**: Undetected utility-bill errors over-charge; mitigated by bill validation
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/IoT (links to VS-20.3/VS-27.2); IT security (links to VS-27.3); utility billing (links to W111); finance/GL (links to VS-17); BI/data (links to VS-28.1); ESG (links to VS-25); data quality (links to VS-28.2)

steps.activity: EEO/Facilities-IT deploy and maintain the energy-metering and data infrastructure: sub-metering of significant energy uses (HVAC, refrigeration, lighting, equipment), IoT/EMS data capture, and integration to the energy-accounting/BI platform (links to VS-28.1) for ~205 sites

EEO/Finance manage energy accounting: capture utility (electricity, fuel, gas, water) consumption and cost per site/entity (links to W111 utility bill processing), validate utility bills, allocate energy cost to sites/entities (links to VS-17/VS-72), and maintain the energy data warehouse

EEO/BI assure energy-data quality (completeness, accuracy, timeliness), manage meter/data gaps, and publish energy-consumption/cost data to analytics (links to W3756), ESG reporting (links to VS-25), and the EnMS (W3740)

fields.Participants: EEO, Procurement (links to VS-34), Treasury (links to VS-18), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Renewable (links to VS-108), Retail Electricity Suppliers (RES)
fields.Trigger: Contract cycle; market change; site addition

workflows.name: Energy Procurement, Retail Competition (RES) & Contract Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "EEO/Procurement manage energy procurement and the retail-competition" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "EEO/Procurement/Treasury manage the energy contract lifecycle and cost" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report energy cost to FP&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-589 (ensure controlled execution — EEC Program Strategy, Designated-Establishment & Governance (PA-120.1).)
- operational: contract structure/hedging; operational: retail-competition strategy
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tariff-exposure risk**: Energy price volatility hits operating cost; mitigated by contract structure/hedging
- **Suboptimal-sourcing risk**: Sites on default tariff vs competitive RES; mitigated by retail-competition strategy
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-34); treasury (links to VS-18); finance (links to VS-17.4); facilities (links to VS-20.3); renewable (links to VS-108); energy data (links to W3741); analytics (links to W3756)

steps.activity: EEO/Procurement manage energy procurement and the retail-competition (RES) strategy under the Philippine Retail Competition and Open Access (RCOA)/Energy Regulatory Commission framework for contestable accounts: source Retail Electricity Suppliers, negotiate contracts (price structure, term, indexation, green/renewable share), and optimize the ~205-account portfolio

EEO/Procurement/Treasury manage the energy contract lifecycle and cost: contract administration, price/volume reconciliation against consumption (links to W3741), market-tariff monitoring (WESM), and demand-response / peak-management where economic

EEO/Finance publish energy-procurement cost analytics, drive sourcing optimization (supplier mix, green tariff, self-generation trade-off links to VS-108), and report energy cost to FP&A (links to VS-17.4) and program analytics (links to W3756)

fields.Participants: EEO, Finance (links to VS-17.4/VS-40), Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Procurement (links to VS-34), PMO (links to VS-112), Sustainability (links to VS-25), Treasury (links to VS-18), Executive (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Annual capex cycle (links to VS-33.1); ECM pipeline; project request
fields.Volume: EEC program budget and ECM capex

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "EEO/Finance develop the EEC program budget and ECM capex" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "EEO/Finance/PMO govern ECM investment decisions" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track ECM investment performance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-138 (ensure RA 11285 energy compliance & M&V integrity.)
- operational: business-case governance; operational: M&V (W3747) and benefits tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-investment risk**: ECM pipeline starved of capex despite positive payback; mitigated by business-case governance
- **Savings-shortfall risk**: Realized savings below business case; mitigated by M&V (W3747) and benefits tracking
System Touchpoints: - Finance/capex (links to VS-40/VS-17.4); facilities (links to VS-20.3); PMO (links to VS-112); renewable (links to VS-108); sustainability (links to VS-25); benefits realization (links to VS-112.3)

steps.activity: EEO/Finance develop the EEC program budget and ECM capex envelope: the operating budget (audit, monitoring, reporting) and the capital envelope for ECM projects (LED retrofit, HVAC upgrade, refrigeration optimization, BMS, renewable links to VS-108), aligned to annual capex planning (links to VS-33.1/VS-40)

EEO/Finance/PMO govern ECM investment decisions: business-case review (payback, IRR, NPV, kWh/PHP saved, GHG reduction), prioritization, approval authority (links to VS-40 capex authority), and stage-gate (links to VS-112 PMO)

EEO/Finance track ECM investment performance: realized savings vs business case, cost/savings reporting to FP&A (links to VS-17.4), and benefits realization (links to VS-112.3); feed to program analytics (links to W3756) and ESG (links to VS-25)

fields.Participants: EEO, Compliance (links to VS-22), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Records (links to VS-88), Audit (links to VS-21), Sustainability (links to VS-25), Finance (links to VS-17)
